correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(H=x_3+x_1^2/(2a)\) and \(\dot H=b-x_1^2\) exactly. Boundedness makes the endpoint correction divided by time vanish, proving the long-time mean-square law and excluding negative forcing. At zero forcing, recurrence returns the continuous nonincreasing H to its initial value, forcing \(x_1\equiv0\), then the vector field forces \(x_2=x_4=0\) and constant \(x_3\). For compact invariant measures, the Lie derivatives of \(x_4,x_1,H,x_3\) give the four stated moment identities. Positive variance and zero mean force both signs; periodic-orbit RMS then gives the zero crossing and amplitude lower bound.
